knowledge:
- key_parameters: design=formula specifying the model where nonlinear continuous covariates must be wrapped in s() ;; gamma=numeric value controlling the smoothness of the nonlinear function in NBAMSeq() (default is 2.5) ;; fitlin=logical indicating whether a linear model should be fitted after fitting the nonlinear model ;; parallel=logical indicating whether parallel processing should be used via BiocParallel ;; name=character string specifying the continuous covariate of interest when pulling out results using results() ;; contrast=character vector of length 3 specifying the factor variable, numerator level, and denominator level for discrete covariates in results() ;; phenoname=character string specifying the phenotype of interest in makeplot() ;; genename=character string specifying the gene of interest in makeplot()
- alternatives: DESeq2, edgeR, NBPSeq, or BBSeq should be preferred if all covariates are assumed to have linear effects on gene counts (i.e. no nonlinear covariates are specified in the design formula).
- when_to_use: When performing differential expression analysis on RNA-Seq count data where at least one continuous covariate of interest (e.g. age, clinical score, time) is expected to have a nonlinear relationship with gene expression.
- pitfalls: The design formula must contain at least one nonlinear covariate wrapped in s() (purely linear designs are not supported) ;; nonlinear covariates cannot be discrete variables or factors ;; design matrices are not supported (only formulas) ;; the sample order in colData must match the column order of countData.

workflows.name: nbamseq_differential_expression
workflows.intent: Perform differential expression analysis of RNA-Seq data with nonlinear covariates, extract results, and visualize the associations.
input: countData (matrix of raw integer gene counts)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare count matrix and sample metadata ;; 2. Define design formula with at least one nonlinear covariate using s() ;; 3. Construct NBAMSeqDataSet ;; 4. Run differential expression analysis using NBAMSeq() ;; 5. Extract results for nonlinear, linear, or discrete covariates using results() ;; 6. Visualize nonlinear associations using makeplot() or custom ggplot2 plotting with size factors from getsf()
workflows.code:
library(NBAMSeq)
n = 50  ## n stands for number of genes
m = 20   ## m stands for sample size
countData = matrix(rnbinom(n*m, mu=100, size=1/3), ncol = m) + 1
mode(countData) = "integer"
colnames(countData) = paste0("sample", 1:m)
rownames(countData) = paste0("gene", 1:n)
pheno = runif(m, 20, 80)
var1 = rnorm(m)
var2 = rnorm(m)
var3 = rnorm(m)
var4 = as.factor(sample(c(0,1,2), m, replace = TRUE))
colData = data.frame(pheno = pheno, var1 = var1, var2 = var2,
    var3 = var3, var4 = var4)
rownames(colData) = paste0("sample", 1:m)
design = ~ s(pheno) + var1 + var2 + var3 + var4
gsd = NBAMSeqDataSet(countData = countData, colData = colData, design = design)
library(BiocParallel)
gsd = NBAMSeq(gsd, parallel = TRUE)
res1 = results(gsd, name = "pheno")
res2 = results(gsd, name = "var1")
res3 = results(gsd, contrast = c("var4", "2", "0"))
makeplot(gsd, phenoname = "pheno", genename = "gene10", main = "gene10")
res1 = res1[order(res1$pvalue),]
topgene = rownames(res1)[1]  
sf = getsf(gsd)
countnorm = t(t(countData)/sf)
library(ggplot2)
setTitle = topgene
df = data.frame(pheno = pheno, logcount = log2(countnorm[topgene,]+1))
ggplot(df, aes(x=pheno, y=logcount))+geom_point(shape=19,size=1)+
    geom_smooth(method='loess')+xlab("pheno")+ylab("log(normcount + 1)")+
    annotate("text", x = max(df$pheno)-5, y = max(df$logcount)-1, 
    label = paste0("edf: ", signif(res1[topgene,"edf"],digits = 4)))+
    ggtitle(setTitle)+
    theme(text = element_text(size=10), plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
